newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products end steady to firm, gasoline tigh.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products end steady to firm, gasoline tigh.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products ended steady to higher with gasoline supplies seen tight until March.
Gasoline prices rose $1-$2 on the back of steady crude oil futures, firmer NYMEX gasoline prices and signs of healthy demand from Africa for low and middle octane material.
The arb stayed shut to the U.S. but no Med cargoes were available for the rest of February, keeping supply tight.
"There is nothing available to March...It is pretty tight in the Med," said one trader.
"Africa is not accustomed to these higher prices and they are flexible to defer (purchases)."
A trader bid $212 fob for leaded but she said the market was closer to $210, putting premium unleaded at $213/$214.
Naphtha was steady tracking a squeeze in the NWE market.
Gas oil was attracting more buying interest as traders worked through potential arbitrage opportunities.
"The arb out of the Med is open and there is also some interest in the east Med," said one trader.

A dual market has developed with the larger 45,000 tonne cargo attracting a higher premiums, of around fob high quote +$4-5 a tonne against smaller lots (with premiums pegged as low as +$1) because of their flexibility to move out of the region.
High sulphur fuel oil was little changed in lacklustre markets, traders said. Low sulphur fuel was also steady, amid a continued lack of enquiry except from traders.
A Turkish tender to buy 50,000 tonnes of low sulphur fuel oil is likely to be covered from outside the region, traders said.
Talk of run cuts at various refineries around Europe is underpinning the market for straight-run fuel oil.
